o.norm: Consonants from the same code group separated by W or H are treated as one.
From http://www.archives.gov/research_room/genealogy/census/soundex.html: Ashcraft is coded A-261 (A, 2 for the S, C ignored, 6 for the R, 1 for the F). It is not coded A-226.

i.norm: Verifies the Soundex "H/W rule": when two consonants that share the same Soundex code are separated only by an {@code H} or a {@code W}, they are collapsed into a single code digit rather than being encoded twice.

Consonants from the same code group separated by W or H are treated as one.

Example taken from the US National Archives Soundex guide (http://www.archives.gov/research_room/genealogy/census/soundex.html): "Ashcraft" is coded A-261, not A-226. The breakdown is:

  • A → retained as the leading letter
  • S → 2
  • C → ignored (same code "2" as S, separated only by the silent H)
  • R → 6
  • F → 1
"sh" and "c" share code 2; the H must not let C produce a second 2.
"yehudit": vowels/H are dropped, leaving Y + D(3) + T(3) collapsed.
"yhwdyt": the H and W are silent and do not separate the consonants.
